vpx_note: VPX 5436's own settings (`src/core/Settings_properties.inl`), in its order. A table's `<table>.ini` beside it may hold any of them for that table alone, as VPX's does. Besides these, VPX 5436 makes settings as devices and actions appear — the input mappings (`[Input]` `Mapping.<action>`, `Mapping.Nudge<n>.…`, `Mapping.Plunger<n>.…`, `Device.<id>.…`) a table's options (`[TableOption]`), and its audio sources' gains (`[Player]` `AudioSource.<plugin>.Gain`, 0 to 2: ours reads PinMAME's, AltSound's, PUP's and WMP's, which the pause menu sets): ours reads them under the same names. VPX 10.8.0's older names that 5436 replaced (its joystick axis and button settings among them) aren't read: bringing a 10.8.0 settings file over belongs to the first setup.
plugins_note: The settings VPX 5436's plugins declare (`plugins/*`), under `[Plugin.<name>]`. Ours plays everything those plugins do itself, so a plugin's `Enable` switches our part off where that makes sense.

Version.VPinball: the VPX version that saved the file
Editor.EnableLog: a log file of the player's own, with the settings screen; it prints to its console now
Editor.DisableHash: VPX's check of a table file's signature; ours reads tables without it
Editor.ThrowBallsAlwaysOn: VPX's debugging tools for throwing and steering balls, not built
Editor.BallControlAlwaysOn: VPX's debugging tools for throwing and steering balls, not built
Editor.*: VPX's editor's own settings — windows, grids, dialogs; ours plays tables and has no editor yet
CVEdit.*: the look of VPX's script editor; ours has none yet (a simple one is planned)
RecentDir.*: the editor's recent folders and files; our library keeps its own
DefaultProps*: the values VPX's editor gives a new part; ours has no editor
DefaultCamera.*: the views VPX's editor gives a new table; ours has no editor
Player.SoundDeviceBG: the backglass's sound output, by name (`vpi-player --sound-outputs`)
Player.SoundDevice: the playfield's sound output, by name
Player.Playfield*: the table's window: screen, place, size, borderless full screen
Player.PlayfieldFSWidth: a display mode for VPX's exclusive full screen, which its BGFX build — like ours — doesn't have (windowed or borderless only)
Backglass.*: the backglass window: off, its own window, or drawn inside the table's
Backglass.BackglassFS*: exclusive full screen's display mode, as above
Player.SyncMode: none, vertical sync, adaptive sync or frame pacing: adaptive sync draws as vertical sync, SDL having no adaptive mode; with nothing set, ours stays fastest, tearing allowed, at most 240 frames a second
Player.MaxFramerate: worked out against the screen's refresh rate as VPX does
Player.MaxPrerenderedFrames: the frames the graphics card may queue, 1 to 3 (1, VPX's default and ours)
Player.GfxBackend: the graphics library VPX's BGFX build draws through; ours draws through SDL's on Direct3D 12
Player.ShowFPS: our readout shown or not (ours has one readout for VPX's two kinds)
Player.SSRefl: VPX's additive screen-space reflections, not ported yet (off by default in VPX)
Player.ForceAnisotropicFiltering: the parts' pictures read anisotropically, or trilinearly when off
Player.CompressTextures: pictures compressed on the graphics card as a table loads, for speed (off by default in VPX)
Player.DynamicAO: ambient occlusion every frame, or made once into the still parts
Player.PFReflection: the most a mirror reflects, VPX's six modes
Player.MaxTexDimension: pictures above a size shrunk as a table loads, for small graphics cards (none shrunk by default on a desktop)
Player.AlphaRampAccuracy: VPX's detail level for rubbers, ramps and balls, drawn and in the physics as VPX takes it (VPX's low-detail ball below 10)
Player.BGSet: the view: desktop, cabinet or full single screen; for one table on its Settings window
Player.CabinetAutofitMode: VPX 5436's automatic cabinet view fitting, not ported yet (manual by default in VPX)
Player.MSAASamples: multisampling; VPX's 6 samples draws with 8, SDL having no 6 (VPX 5436's BGFX build has none either and draws without)
Player.BallAntiStretch: a ball squeezed back against the view's stretching, as VPX does it
Player.BallTrail: VPX's legacy ball trails, not ported (off by default; VPX means to replace them with motion blur, which ours has)
Player.OverwriteBallImage: the player's own pictures for every ball
Player.BallImage: as above: the ball's room picture, read as a sphere map
Player.TouchOverlay: touch screens' controls on phones and tablets
Player.EnableCameraModeFlyAround: moving the camera from VPX's in-game menu, which ours doesn't have yet
Player.DetectHang: a script that hangs found and reported; with the settings screen
Player.SecurityLevel: VPX's levels of what scripts may do; ours fences every script instead, a stricter mode planned
Player.Mirror: the whole table mirrored left to right, not built
Player.CacheMode: VPX's cache of its pictures for faster loading; ours loads its own way
Player.MinPhysLoopTime: a legacy delay VPX's BGFX build doesn't have either
Player.PhysicsMaxLoops: VPX's limit on catching up when a slow machine falls behind; ours keeps up on its own thread
Player.Autostart: VPX starting a table by itself after a while; front ends launch tables
Player.Exitconfirm: a long press of Esc to leave, with an in-game menu for the short press
Input.Devices: the devices the mappings name, and each one's automatic layout switch (`Device.<id>.NoAutoLayout`); the list itself is for the settings screen
Player.KeyboardNudgeMode: VPX's three keyboard nudges; ours defaults to the released VPX's
Player.NudgeStrength: how far a nudge shakes the picture
Player.PlungerRetract: a plunger pulled by a key eases forward again after a second
Player.PlungerNormalize: VPX 5436 defines it but nothing in it reads it
Player.FlipperPhysics*: VPX's eight physics sets — flippers' and the table's values, and each set's name — for tables and flippers that choose one
Player.TablePhysics*: VPX's eight physics sets — flippers' and the table's values, and each set's name — for tables and flippers that choose one
Player.PhysicsSetName*: VPX's eight physics sets — flippers' and the table's values, and each set's name — for tables and flippers that choose one
Player.ScreenWidth: the cabinet screen's size, for VPX's window view
Player.ScreenHeight: used only by the cabinet autofit and VR, not built
Player.ScreenPlayerX: where the player stands, for VPX's window view
Player.OverrideTableEmissionScale: the player's light level over the table's; for one table on its Settings window, as VPX 5436's in-game menu offers it ("Scene lighting")
Player.EmissionScale: the player's light level, day to night
Player.DynamicDayNight: the light level from the sun where the player lives, now, as VPX works it out
TableOverride.View*: the views' settings over the table's
TableOverride.Difficulty: the player's difficulty for the table, on its Settings window
TableOverride.Exposure: the player's exposure for the table, on its Settings window
TableOverride.ToneMapper: the player's tone mapper for the table, on its Settings window
DMD.*: VPX's seven DMD looks for the score view
Controller.*: the cabinet's toy choices that tables' `controller.vbs` reads
Plugin.B2SLegacy.Enable: which of VPX's two B2S plugins draws; ours is one, VPX 5436's newer one
Plugin.DMDUtil.Enable: a real DMD panel through libdmdutil
Plugin.FlexDMD.Enable: in VPX it chooses its plugin or the installed FlexDMD; ours is always our own port
Plugin.PinMAME.Enable: in VPX it chooses its plugin or the installed VPinMAME; ours always runs PinMAME itself
Plugin.ScoreView.Enable: VPX's score view layouts on or off
Plugin.WMP.Enable: in VPX it chooses its plugin or Windows Media Player itself; ours is always the stand-in
Standalone.*: VPX's builds for phones, tablets and Linux
Plugin.AltSound.Folder: where AltSound packs are, besides beside the table
Plugin.B2S.ShowGrill: the backglass picture's speaker grill shown
Plugin.B2S.ScoreViewDMD*: the DMD over the backglass file's score panel: off, found by itself, or placed
Plugin.B2S.BackglassDMD*: the DMD over the backglass: likewise
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SHideGrill: the grill hidden, when the newer plugin's `ShowGrill` isn't set
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SHideB2SDMD: the backglass file's score panel left out
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SHideB2SBackglass: the backglass file left out while a PinUP pack still draws there; for now `[Backglass]` `BackglassOutput = 0` turns the window off
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SHideDMD: VPX 5436 defines it but nothing in it reads it
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SDualMode: two-mode backglasses (authentic and fantasy), with B2S Server's other extras
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SBackglass*: the legacy plugin's own window sizes; ours takes the backglass window's
Plugin.B2SLegacy.B2SDMD*: as above, for its DMD window
Plugin.DMDUtil.*: handed to libdmdutil as VPX's plugin hands them
Plugin.Inspector.*: VPX's web page for looking inside a running table, a developer's tool
Plugin.PinMAME.Sound: the machines' sound on or off
Plugin.PinMAME.PinMAMEPath: a PinMAME folder of the user's own: its `roms` and `samples`, after a `pinmame` folder beside the table, as VPX 5436 looks
Plugin.PinMAME.Cheat: PinMAME's cheat mode, which skips some games' start-up tests
Plugin.PUP.BGPad*: the backglass window's padding, the pack's screens drawn inside it
Plugin.PUP.BGFrameOverlay: VPX 5436 defines it but never registers or reads it
Plugin.PUP.PUPFolder: a PinUP folder of the user's own, its `PUPVideos` holding the packs
Plugin.RemoteControl.*: VPX's remote control between two of its own copies, a developer's tool

vpi.label: A sound for each achievement
vpi.what: Whether a sound plays as each achievement is announced: the pack's own, or the player's chime (Settings › Sound).

vpi.label: The achievements' sound level
vpi.what: The level of the sound played as an achievement is announced, over the backglass volume, from 0 to 2: one of the pause menu's sound levels (Settings › Sound too).

vpi.label: The table's music level
vpi.what: The level of a table's own music, what its script plays with PlayMusic, over the backglass volume, from 0 to 2: one of the pause menu's sound levels, beside the machine's, AltSound's, PinUP's and Media Player's ([Player] AudioSource.….Gain).

vpi.label: How frames reach the screen
opts: Drawn just before the refresh that shows them (paced)
vpi.what: How frames reach the screen: as soon as each is drawn (immediate, which can tear), tear-free without waiting (mailbox), in the display's queue (vsync), or each drawn just before the refresh that shows it (paced); empty, as [Player] SyncMode says.

vpi.label: The score display floating over the table
vpi.what: On one screen, a ROM table's score display floats over the table while its script leaves PinMAME's window shown.

vpi.label: The other windows shown from the start
vpi.what: The backglass, score and topper windows show as the table starts; off, each shows with its first picture.

vpi.label: Tilt by counting nudges
vpi.what: A tilt comes from counting presses of the nudge keys, in place of the tilt bob's swing.

vpi.label: HDR on screens with HDR on
vpi.what: An HDR picture (HDR10) on a screen with Windows' HDR on; off, ordinary colors there too.

vpi.label: The score window in the HDR look
vpi.what: On an HDR screen, the score window in the HDR look; off, in its true colors.

vpi.label: A display device for a real DMD
vpi.what: A display device for a real DMD panel: the path of its DmdDevice64.dll (DMD Extensions', or a panel maker's), or 1 for the one in VPinMAME's folder; empty, none.

vpi.label: The display device's settings file
vpi.what: The display device's own settings file (its DmdDevice.ini); empty, the one beside it.

vpi.label: Esc opens the pause menu first
vpi.what: Esc (or Q) opens the pause menu with Quit the table picked; off, Esc ends play at once. A front end that starts a table with -minimized always gets the at-once end.

vpi.label: The screens layout tables play with
vpi.what: One of the Screens page's saved layouts, by its name; a table's own settings can name another.

vpi.label: A screenshot at a high score
vpi.what: A screenshot when a game makes the high scores — a ROM machine's in its memory, or a table script's own when it saves a new one — into the table's screenshots.

vpi.label: The windows a screenshot takes
vpi.what: The windows a screenshot takes: playfield, backglass, dmd and topper, separated by commas; empty, every window that shows.

vpi.label: Tables may reach outside their files
vpi.what: Tables' scripts may reach outside their own files — the internet, other programs, every file — as some tables' online features need; off, each script keeps to its table's own files. A table's own line in a [ScriptsReachOutside] section, its file's name = 1 or 0, counts over this for that table.

vpi.label: The library's tables folder
vpi.what: The folder holding the library's tables, which first setup sets; the app and the player read the library from it.

vpi.label: The library's scripts folder
vpi.what: The folder of the scripts tables load (core.vbs, controller.vbs and the machines' own); empty, the Scripts folder beside the tables folder.

vpi.label: The library's PinUP packs folder
vpi.what: The folder holding the library's PinUP packs (PinUP's PUPVideos); empty, the one found above the tables.

vpi.label: How the library keeps its tables
vpi.what: game: each game in a folder of its own, its versions sharing it, as Visual Pinball X 10.8.1 keeps tables; empty, VPX's shared folders. The app's Library settings switch between them, moving the files.

vpi.label: PinballX's folder
vpi.what: Where PinballX is installed, for putting a table's media where it shows them; empty, its usual folders are looked in.

vpi.label: PinballY's folder
vpi.what: Where PinballY is installed, for putting a table's media where it shows them; empty, its usual folders are looked in.
